t: A Lozi kingdom on the upper Zambezi floodplain, ruled by the Litunga with a princess-chief governing the south from Nalolo.
Kololo invaders from the south ruled the floodplain for a generation until the Lozi restored their kingdom in 1864.
Lewanika’s treaties with Rhodes’s company kept Barotseland’s king and councils alive under British rule until 1964.
dyk: Silozi, the language of the Lozi kingdom, is mainly derived from Sotho, the speech of the Kololo who ruled the floodplain for only about 25 years.
ev: Mulambwa becomes Litunga and extends the kingdom’s tribute over neighbouring peoples
The Kololo under Sebitwane conquer the floodplain
Sipopa leads a Lozi rising that ends Kololo rule
Lubosi, later called Lewanika, becomes Litunga
Lewanika signs the Lochner Concession with the British South Africa Company
Italian arbitration fixes the border with Angola, cutting off western lands
The Barotseland Agreement brings the kingdom into independent Zambia
Zambia abrogates the agreement and renames the area Western Province

f.capital: Northern floodplain royal villages; later Lealui (flood season: Limulunga)
f.predecessor: Luyi chiefdoms of the Bulozi floodplain
